title: File handling
sub: Worksheet for the 360° experience: Records office
objectives: know how to open a text file, read what is in it and close it again
understand the difference between write mode and append mode
know how to split one line of a file into its separate fields
starter: A program opens scores.txt in write mode, and the file already holds 40 lines of results. Write down what the file holds the moment that line has run, and which mode should have been used to add to it instead.

stations.name: Reading a whole file
stations.fact: A file left open can keep other programs out, and may lose data that was not written yet.
stations.challenge: Why should a program close a file as soon as it has finished with it?

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: A file called notice.txt is already there. Read the whole of it in one go, close it, and display exactly what was in it and nothing of your own.
A file called log.txt is already there and may be empty. Read it and count every character, newlines included, then display characters [the count].

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Reading line by line
stations.fact: A newline is one single invisible character, which is why a stripped line comes out shorter.
stations.challenge: Why is a stripped line one character shorter than the line that was read?

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program
Marks
Done
rows: A file called rota.txt is already there and may be empty. Read its first line only, close the file and strip the newline off, then display first [that line], then length [how many characters] on the next line.
A file called names.txt is already there with one name per line, and may be empty. Read it and display lines [how many lines], then one line per name in the form [position] [name], counting from 1.

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Writing to a file
stations.fact: Write mode creates the file if it is not there, which is handy and dangerous in equal measure.
stations.challenge: What happens to the contents of a file the moment it is opened in w mode?

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program

rows: Ask the user for a title. Make a file called report.txt, write the title on one line and ready on the next, and close it. Then read report.txt back in one go and display it.

Ask the user for an entry. Open the file stock.txt in write mode, which empties whatever it held, write that entry on a line of its own and close it. Read it back and display [every line], then lines [how many].

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Adding to a file
stations.fact: Three modes cover everything you need: r to read, w to write from scratch and a to add on the end.
stations.challenge: Which mode would a visitor log use, and why that one?

rows: Ask the user for a name and append it to the file visits.txt on a line of its own, without losing the names already there. Then read the whole file back and display latest [the last name], then total [how many lines].

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Records in a file
stations.fact: A file of comma-separated records is a CSV file, and a spreadsheet will open one straight away.
stations.challenge: How does a program find the record for one particular name?

logic.title: Tick each one off as its tests pass in the editor
head: Program

Done
rows: Ask the user for a name to find in the file members.txt, which holds one name,age record per line. Look at every record and display [name] is [age], or not a member when none matches, then checked [how many you looked at].

A file called scores.txt is already there, holding one name,score record per line, and may be empty. Read it and display no scores when it holds none, or total [every score added up], then best [the highest scorer's name].

logic.title: Plan the one you found hardest: inputs, what happens to them, what is printed.

stations.name: Putting it together
stations.fact: Skipping blank lines is worth doing every time: a stray newline at the end of a file is very common.
stations.challenge: Plan the two files a sales report program would need.

Ask the user for a limit. The file readings.txt holds one sensor,reading record per line: make a file called alerts.txt holding a line of [sensor] [reading] for each reading above the limit. Then read alerts.txt back and display [every line], then alerts [how many].

keyq: Why does the mode a file is opened in matter more than anything else on that line?
exam: Every line read from a file is measured with len(), and each answer comes out one character bigger than expected. Name the character being counted, and write the line that removes it.
Write a program that adds a new visitor's name onto the end of log.txt without losing the names already in it, and then prints the whole file.
Each line of members.txt holds a name and an age, separated by a comma. Write a program that prints the name of every member aged 16 or over.
